issues.problem: पीपर is a regional name and is confusable with पीपल (Ficus religiosa); the ordinary Hindi name of pippalī (long pepper) is पिप्पली (also पीपली/छोटी पीपर).
English says 'grape or raisin'; in a kalka the dried grape (मुनक्का) is the usual understanding, Hindi names only the fresh grape.

Hindi and English state madhuka = liquorice, but here tvacaḥ may govern the whole list (as noted for unit 68), and with 'skins' the madhūka tree (mahua, Madhuca longifolia) is a possible alternative reading; the unit's notes carry no scope note or hedge.

patch.text: Scope of tvacaḥ is ambiguous (it may govern madhuka and uduṃbara, or only uduṃbara). madhuka = liquorice is probable (as in units 45, 60), but if tvacaḥ governs it, the bark of the madhūka tree (mahua) is a possible alternative; uduṃbara = Ficus racemosa, cluster fig (standard); śarkarā = sugar, kṣaudra = honey (standard).
